rubrics.rubric: Does the response correctly identify that the measured efficiency at rated flow (68.2%) fails the pump datasheet's guaranteed minimum efficiency of 72%?
criterion: The response must identify that the guaranteed minimum efficiency per the pump specification datasheet is 72% at rated flow (180 m³/h).
The response must state the measured efficiency at Test Point 6 as 68.2%, which is 3.8 percentage points below the guaranteed value.

The response must attribute the 72% minimum efficiency requirement to the pump datasheet. API 610 12th Edition treats efficiency guarantees and tolerances as purchaser-specified requirements, so the datasheet's guarantee must not be presented as a universal API 610 minimum-efficiency rule.
The response must present a clear pass/fail determination with the specific numerical values from the test data and specification.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response explicitly acknowledge that ISO 10816-3:2009 excluded rotodynamic pumps from its scope (transferred to ISO 10816-7) and discuss this standards conflict?
criterion: The response must explicitly state that ISO 10816-3:2009 (second edition) removed rotodynamic pumps from its scope, as noted in its Foreword, with pumps now dealt with in ISO 10816-7.
The response must reference the Europump guidelines (Section 1.4.1) confirming that ISO 10816-3 is no longer the vibration standard for pumps and has been superseded by Part 7.

The response must discuss the standards conflict — that the specification may reference ISO 10816-3 but it no longer applies to pumps — and explain that ISO 10816-7 is the correct pump-specific standard.
Simply applying ISO 10816-3 classifications without acknowledging this exclusion fails this criterion.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response correctly classify the pump under ISO 10816-7 as Category II and apply the appropriate zone boundaries for ≤200 kW pumps?
criterion: The response must classify the pump as Category II under ISO 10816-7, with rationale that it is a raw water transfer pump at a water treatment plant (non-hazardous liquid, general application).
The response must note the pump is rated at 75 kW (≤200 kW), which determines the applicable zone boundary set.
The correct zone boundaries for Category II ≤200 kW must be stated: Zone A ≤3.2 mm/s, Zone B ≤5.1 mm/s, Zone C ≤8.5 mm/s, Zone D >8.5 mm/s.
Using Category I limits or ISO 10816-3 Group 2 limits instead would be incorrect.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response correctly calculate bearing defect frequencies (BPFO, BPFI, BSF, FTF) for the SKF 6313 C3 (DE) bearing using appropriate geometric parameters and the actual test speed?
criterion: The response must use the standard bearing defect frequency formulas: BPFO = (Z/2)×fs×(1−Dw/Dm×cos α), BPFI = (Z/2)×fs×(1+Dw/Dm×cos α), BSF = (Dm/(2×Dw))×fs×(1−(Dw/Dm×cos α)²), FTF = (fs/2)×(1−Dw/Dm×cos α).
The response must use correct geometric parameters for SKF 6313: Z=8 balls, Dw≈22.23 mm, Dm≈102.5 mm, contact angle α=0°, at actual test speed ~2968 RPM / 49.47 Hz.
The calculated results must be approximately: BPFO ≈ 155 Hz, BPFI ≈ 241 Hz, BSF ≈ 109 Hz, FTF ≈ 19.4 Hz (minor variations in geometric parameters are acceptable).
The response must also calculate defect frequencies for the NDE bearing (SKF 6311 C3).

rubrics.rubric: Does the response cross-reference the calculated bearing defect frequencies against the FFT spectrum data and determine whether bearing defect signatures are present?
criterion: The response must compare calculated bearing defect frequencies (BPFO ≈ 155 Hz, BPFI ≈ 241 Hz, BSF ≈ 109 Hz for the 6313) against the FFT spectral data at both rated and 120% flow conditions.
The response must assess the elevated amplitude (~0.17 mm/s) near 149 Hz in the rated flow spectrum relative to the DE bearing (SKF 6313) BPFO region (~155 Hz).
The response must distinguish between genuine bearing defect signatures (discrete peaks at defect frequencies with potential sidebands at shaft frequency) and coincidental spectral energy.
Simply listing calculated frequencies without cross-referencing them against actual spectral data is insufficient.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response identify the 1× running speed peak (~49.5 Hz) as the dominant spectral component and note the amplitude increase from rated flow (~1.73 mm/s) to 120% flow (~2.72 mm/s)?
criterion: The response must identify the dominant 1× running speed peak at approximately 49.5 Hz in the FFT spectra, with amplitude of approximately 1.73 mm/s at rated flow and 2.72 mm/s at 120% flow (a ~57% increase).
The response must note the 2× harmonic at ~99 Hz also shows significant presence (0.65 mm/s at rated, 1.24 mm/s at 120%).

The response should explain that while a dominant 1× component typically indicates unbalance or misalignment, in the context of a factory acceptance test with dramatically different behavior at different flow rates, hydraulic loading effects (increased radial thrust at off-BEP flows) are the more likely cause.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response present a speed-corrected performance comparison table showing raw measured, affinity-law-corrected, rated specification values, and pass/fail determination for head, power, and efficiency at rated flow?
criterion: The response must present a clear tabular format (as explicitly requested in the task instructions) for at least the rated flow point (180 m³/h).
The table must include raw measured values from the Performance Data sheet: Head=30.8 m, Power=58.5 kW, Efficiency=68.2% at 2968 RPM.
The table must include affinity-law-corrected values to 2970 RPM and rated specification values (Head=45 m, Power=58 kW, Efficiency=72%).

The table must include pass/fail determination against the head and power tolerances (Head ±3%, Power +4%) and the datasheet's separately specified minimum guaranteed efficiency of 72%, identifying the source of each requirement.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response document vibration acceptance and limit applicability for all 7 test points, applying the 3.0 mm/s limit within the specified preferred operating range and the 3.9 mm/s limit outside it but within the specified allowable operating range?
criterion: The response must document all 7 test points and apply the vibration limits using the operating ranges specified in the pump datasheet: 3.0 mm/s RMS within the preferred operating range (126–198 m³/h: Test Points 4, 5, 6) and 3.9 mm/s RMS outside the preferred range but within the allowable operating range (54–216 m³/h: Test Points 2, 3, 7).

Test Points 2–5 must be identified as passing on both DE and NDE bearings. Test Point 1 is shutoff (0 m³/h), outside the specified allowable operating range: retain its measured readings but mark the POR/AOR vibration-limit assessment as not applicable, with a justification. Low readings alone do not establish acceptable continuous operation at shutoff; an unqualified API 610 vibration-acceptance pass for this point is not sufficient.
Test Point 6 (100% BEP) must be identified as failing on DE (3.5 > 3.0) but passing on NDE (2.5 ≤ 3.0).
Test Point 7 (120% BEP) must be identified as failing on both DE (5.8 > 3.9) and NDE (4.3 > 3.9).

rubrics.rubric: Does the response reconcile vibration classification across API 610 and ISO 10816-7 using the Europump guidelines as a bridging reference, rather than treating the standards in isolation?
criterion: The response must use the Europump Pump Vibration Standards Guidelines as a reconciling document to bridge API 610 (ISO 13709) acceptance criteria with ISO 10816-7 severity zone classification.

The response must compare API 610 limits (Overall: POR 3.0 mm/s, AOR 3.9 mm/s; Discrete: POR 2.0 mm/s, AOR 2.6 mm/s) with ISO 10816-7 zone boundaries (for Category II ≤200 kW: Zone A ≤3.2, Zone B ≤5.1, Zone C ≤8.5, Zone D >8.5 mm/s).

The response should note that the API 610 preferred operating range limit of 3.0 mm/s is close to the ISO 10816-7 Zone A/B boundary of 3.2 mm/s for Category II pumps, demonstrating consistency between the standards.
The analysis must show how the two standards complement each other rather than treating them in isolation.
